problem_text: Is it possible to choose 1983 distinct positive integers, all less than or equal to 10^5, no three of which are consecutive terms of an arithmetic progression? Justify your answer.
solution_text: Yes. Define base_two_to_base_three(n) as the number obtained by writing n in binary and reinterpreting the digit string in base 3. Consider the set S = {base_two_to_base_three(n) : 1 <= n <= 2^k - 1} for k = 11. (1) |S| = 2^11 - 1 = 2047 >= 1983 since base_two_to_base_three is injective. (2) Each element of S has only digits 0 and 1 in base 3, so each is at most 1 + 3 + 9 + ... + 3^10 = (3^11 - 1)/2 = 88573 < 10^5. (3) No three elements form an AP: if x, y, z in S with x + z = 2y, then in base 3, each digit of x and z is 0 or 1, so x + z has no carry and each digit is 0, 1, or 2. Meanwhile 2y has digits 0 or 2 (doubling 0 or 1 in base 3, no carry). So x + z = 2y forces each digit of x + z to be 0 or 2, meaning each digit of x equals the corresponding digit of z, hence x = z, contradicting x < y < z. Taking any 1983 elements of S gives the desired set.
solution_summary: Reinterpret binary digits as base-3 digits to construct an AP-free set of size 2047 with all elements <= 88573 < 10^5; take any 1983 of them.
answer: Yes, it is possible. The construction uses base-2 to base-3 digit reinterpretation: take any 1983 numbers from {base_two_to_base_three(n) : 1 <= n <= 2^11 - 1}, giving 2047 distinct positive integers all <= (3^11-1)/2 = 88573 < 10^5 with no three forming an arithmetic progression.
